kwargs.content:
CLAIMANT POSITION SUMMARY
Fisher v. AutoMax
AAA Case No. M-2024-506
Prepared for Mandatory Pre-Hearing Exchange

I. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

Claimant Sandra Fisher purchased a new vehicle from AutoMax. The vehicle experienced a persistent transmission nonconformity that substantially impairs its use, value, and safety. Ms. Fisher presented the vehicle for repair on four separate occasions for the same transmission defect, none of which resulted in a successful repair.

II. LEGAL BASIS - MOTOR VEHICLE WARRANTY ENFORCEMENT ACT

Sandra Fisher's four failed repair attempts for the same transmission nonconformity establish the presumption under the Motor Vehicle Warranty Enforcement Act. Under the Act's statutory presumption, four unsuccessful repair attempts for the same nonconformity conclusively establish that the vehicle is a lemon and the manufacturer/dealer is liable for full remedies.

III. EXPERT ANALYSIS

Claimant's automotive engineer expert has opined that the transmission defect is a manufacturing defect that cannot be remedied through standard repair procedures. The expert's analysis confirms the transmission nonconformity is a fundamental design/manufacturing flaw affecting the entire transmission assembly.

IV. ARBITRATION STRATEGY AND POSITION

Claimant will establish at arbitration that: (1) the four failed repair attempts trigger the statutory lemon law presumption; (2) AutoMax failed to cure the defect within a reasonable number of attempts; (3) the transmission nonconformity substantially impairs the vehicle's use and value; and (4) Claimant is entitled to full statutory remedies.

V. DAMAGES CALCULATION

Damages include purchase price, finance charges, and attorney fees under the fee-shifting statute. Specifically:
- Full vehicle purchase price refund
- All finance charges paid
- Incidental and consequential damages
- Attorney fees and costs under the fee-shifting provision of the Motor Vehicle Warranty Enforcement Act

Total claimed damages exceed $45,000 inclusive of attorney fees.

Prepared by: Hartwell & Associates
Matter: M-2024-506
Exchange authorized per AAA Pre-Hearing Order
